sections.text: Giving themselves up to insatiable passions, hypocritical, self-sufficient and arrogant, cherishing false conception founded on delusion, they work only to carry out their own unholy purposes.
Poring anxiously over evil resolutions, which only end in death; seeking only the gratification of desire as the highest goal; seeing nothing beyond;
Caught in the toils of a hundred vain hopes, the slaves of passion and wrath, they accumulate hoards of unjust wealth, only to pander to their sensual desire.

We are discussing chapter 16, Deva Asura Sampath Vibhaga Yoga -- Yoga of Divine and Devilish Qualities, or Estate, or Wealth. We have started learning Bhagavad Gita from Lord Krishna, where he first gave us this scenario of Arjuna -- a broken-down hero, a person who has all the strength, all the valor, all the training to fight his situations. But under the burden of the circumstances, he broke down and did not know what to do and what not to do.
So Bhagavan told him that the only cure for your condition is to correct your understanding about what is right and what is wrong, what is permanent and what is impermanent. Since the second chapter, it clearly says that your mistake is that you are identifying with your limited self and looking at all the other people through their limited equipment. But they are imperishable when it comes to the soul.
Their real being is imperishable, just as yours. So that was the correction Bhagavan wanted Arjuna to make the identification from this limited to unlimited. In Bhagavad Gita, the journey is to change your identification from the limited being that I think I am to the unlimited soul that I actually am.
Everything we have discussed so far in Bhagavad Gita is towards that goal -- changing my identification from the limited self to the unlimited self. So entire Bhagavad Gita up to chapter 15 has described that unlimited self and how to identify with that. And in chapter 16 now we are discussing what is that which is binding me to their limited self.
So as we have discussed, the first three verses told us about the qualities of the divine being or the divine estate. As we transact in this world, we are going to acquire wealth, we also accumulate other wealth. Respect, recognition, appreciation, and on the other side, disgust, criticism, all that also we accumulate along with accumulating the wealth which is generally our normal endeavor in life.
So these become our estate. Some are divine and some are devilish. Something which are acquired is pure and something we are called impure.
So Bhagavan gave us the first 26 qualities of the divine estate. And then in the fourth verse he gave another six qualities of the devilish estate. So he said, the divine is quite obvious.
Most of us recognize divinity when we see it. And as we have discussed last time, it is easier for us to find divinity in us. For my mind to detect good quality in me is easy, very difficult for my mind to detect the negative tendencies in me, but it is very easy for my mind to see negative tendencies in others.
That person is very hypocritical. Well, he is doing it for ego only. We can very clearly recognize it, but it is very difficult for us to recognize in ourselves.
So this chapter takes upon itself to describe in detail what would be the behavior of a person who is predominated by negative tendencies, which in this case we call asuric tendencies. So when we see this behavior in others, it is easier to detect. But when I do something similar, I consider that as well very, very minor or well, this is the way the life works.
If I dont do it, then people will trample over me, Ill be a doormat. So my behavior I can justify saying thats how you survive in this world. But Bhagavan makes it very clear that if you detect this type of behavior, this behavior is very negative for your evolution, for your goal of liberation.
So he said there are two types of one helps you to liberate yourself from the limitation. Other will be binding you to this limitation. The more you try to satisfy your desires to get happiness through material goals, the more you will be binding yourself to these limitations.
Pravrittim nivrittim cha janah na viduh asurah. The first indication is that the person does not know what to get engaged in and what to stay away from. I do not know what to do and what not to do -- which is what Arjunas situation was in the very first chapter.
He did not know what is right for him. Bhagawan is not saying the Arjuna is asura, but the behavior he exhibited was clearly of asuric tendency. So something in him which was not allowing him to decide what is right and what is wrong.
But once I know that thats a negative tendency Pravrittimcha nivruttimcha janahanna vidhu asuraha those who have the predominant qualities, they will not know what to do, what not to do. Na saucam, na apiyacharah na satyam teshu vidyate they will not have purity, cleanliness also na satyam teshu vidyate. They will not be able to tell the truth.
And it is not to put them down that Bhagavan is saying this. Its actually somewhat of a pity for them that theyre incapable of doing so. Theyre incapable of living an honest life, incapable of telling the truth.
Because theyre so afraid that telling truth will put them in trouble. In our daily life we call it white lie. Because you know, telling truth is going to put me in trouble.
Well, you really dont want to say what you really think about. They will say generally around looks good. So that basically is my incapacity to tell the truth.
These people, when look at overall life, they are just not capable of telling truth because of their desire to protect what they consider is giving them happiness. And then he continues. Asatyam a pratishtam te jagat ahuhu Anishwaram.
This statement relates to what we have learned so far in Bhagavad Gita. In Bhagavad Gita we have learned that the nature of the self is Sat chit in Ananda that Sat is ever existing. We also learned that Sat truth is something which is consistent in all three periods of time.
In the past, in the present and future. Something which was true in past has to be true today and will also be true tomorrow. So that is considered Sathya.
But that which is not consistent, something which was true yesterday, which is not true today. At some point it was true. Everybody agreed with each other.
Other will all fall down at the edge of the earth. But now we know that thats not true. So that was not true.
Now what we know was true then even though we did not know it. It is true today and will remain true tomorrow. The people with asuric tendencies, they think that this world is asat.
In a sense it is impermanent. It came in existence by chance and will perish. That means its not permanent or pratish.
It just by chance occurring. It happened Te jagat ahuhu an ishwaram. And there is no controller.
There is no central authority who govern the laws of nature. Their view is it all came about by an accident. Will remain in this situation for a while and will disappear.
There is no basis for this world to exist. There is no fundamental substratum which supports this universe. Universe came in Existence by accident will get destroyed by accident, basically.
Or pratishtham te jagat ahu Anishwam. This is the worldview, a person is a materialistic view. When I try to analyze the truth in this nature through pure physical science, only then obviously the only thing I can find is these two came together by some accident.
These elements came together by accident and then it happened this. Then other things happened by accident and then this happened this. So starting from the Big Bang, we can say Big Bang occurred.
Why it occurred we dont know. But its an accident. It occurred and after that it started expanding and then hydrogen became helium.
And all this is just an accident without any basis. Anishwaram There is no controller who is controlling the laws of nature. Aparaha paraha sambhutam.
By coming together two opposites. Kim annyat kaama haithu kam. So the progeny or the continuing of this life on this planet came out by just accident.
By coming two together and for the only purpose fulfilling desire. There was no master plan, there is no underlying truth, there is no substratum. But it just all chance occurring.
This is the view of the materialistic atheistic people. They have no faith in any underlying reality for this world. Etam drastim avastabya nastaatmanaha alpa buddhayaha.
Obviously this is a direct criticism from the Gitacharya that these people are wrong. They are seeing this from a very narrow perspective because they are viewing this world from a very narrow perspective. So when I see my life as a living being and I just analyze from a chemical perspective, electrical perspective, this is just a pure machine.
It came together and it is pumping blood through the pumping action. And I can define everything in a mechanical term, in a physical term, in a chemical term, and say this is me. But what is it that keeping all the systems together, I really dont have an answer.
Simply saying its just all working together. Physics came together, science came together. So basically you can see this life either as something divine which is supporting it, or simply say this is all just chance occurring.
There is a book I have read called Brief History of Almost Everything. Its a fantastic book. It explains right from the Big Bang to where we are today in a very succinct manner.
His conclusion is that we as human beings existing on this planet is almost a chance. That one in a million odds that happen thing and it happened and continue happening and we are still existing. But anything could have gone wrong and we wouldnt have been here.
So basically youre saying that maybe just a chance that we have become who we are. So here Bhagavan is saying that these people are looking at the world from a material perspective, analyzing whats happening from a material perspective. Theyre coming to the conclusion its just chance occurring.
Why I am not tall enough and other guy 7ft tall is just a chance occurring. So Bhagavan said that having such view Nast Atmanah they are destroying their own self because they are negating their own self. They are not even recognizing that there is underlying reality.
Called myself Alpa Buddhaya. They have intellect they are obviously analyzing. They are using all the faculties to understand this world.
But from a very narrow perspective. Alpam Buddha Fools it basically says very narrow perspective. Prabhavanti Ugrakarmanah Shayaya Jagato Ahitah.
So the actions are very harsh because they are not recognizing the underlying unity of our things and being. You can take example of vegetarianism. The one underlying theme of vegetarianism is that every life has right to survive and live.
So you have to inflict as little harm to a life to support yourself. But if I dont have that view, then obviously killing other animals may be justified. So Bhagawan said that because they have a narrow perspective, their actions are harsh.
Shaya Jagato Ahithaha because of the misunderstanding of how this universe work, they are the enemies of the world for its destruction. You can relate to our green movement about saving the planet. Now obviously there are a lot of people coming out saying all this thing is a hoax.
We really dont need to preserve anything. This planet will preserve itself. In fact, I just read that somebody written a book that actually the global warming will be very good for farming.
There are more warmer weather and it will make people rich. So you can look at it from any perspective and your perspective will decide how youre going to act in this world.

Verse 10 describes those driven by dushpuram kamam - insatiable desires. The key word is insatiable. A natural desire (I am thirsty, I drink water) is fulfilled and ends. But obsessive craving (I must have more, bigger, better) can never be satisfied because it arises from an inner emptiness that no external object can fill. The verse also mentions asuchi-vratah - impure resolves, actions taken without consideration of their ethical consequences. Examine your desires today: Which are simple needs that can be met and released? Which are obsessions that keep growing regardless of what you acquire? Choose one insatiable desire and ask: What inner lack am I trying to fill with this external pursuit?
Verses 11-12 paint a vivid picture: those bound by hundreds of ropes of hope (asha-pasha-shataih baddhah), slaves to desire and anger (kama-krodha-parayanah), accumulating wealth through unjust means (anyayena artha-sanchayan). Notice the progression - endless hoping leads to attachment, attachment to frustration, frustration to unethical action. The teaching uses the powerful image of being bound by hundreds of ropes. Each unfulfilled desire is another rope. Each resentment is another knot. Today, identify one rope that binds you - perhaps an expectation about how someone should treat you, or an attachment to a particular outcome. Practice releasing it, not through suppression but through understanding: This hope is creating my bondage. I can act appropriately without being imprisoned by the result.
